title: Endometrial biopsy
what: The doctor passes a thin, flexible tube through the cervix into the womb and takes a little tissue from its lining. No cuts, and usually no anesthesia.
why: For irregular periods, bleeding after menopause, infertility, or when an ultrasound shows a changed womb lining.
duration: the procedure usually takes 5 to 15 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
Any discharge or inflammation right now

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: The cycle day depends on the purpose. Your doctor will say when to come.

prepare.title: Test
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked to take a pregnancy test before the procedure.

prepare.title: Painkiller
prepare.text: Ask your doctor if you can take a painkiller an hour before.

steps: You sit in the gynecological chair
The doctor inserts a speculum and cleans the cervix
A thin, flexible tube is passed through the cervix into the womb
Gentle suction draws up some tissue. It takes a few seconds
The tube is removed, and the tissue is sent to the lab
feel: A strong cramp, like a painful period, usually brief
Sometimes dizziness or nausea. Tell the doctor
Afterward, cramping for a few hours
after: Light bleeding, usually for 1 to 2 days
No sex, tampons, baths, or pools, usually for a few days. Your doctor will say exactly
Your doctor will explain the result at your visit
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), severe pain low in the belly, or bad-smelling discharge

faq.a: You feel a sharp cramp, like a painful period. It is brief, usually under a minute.

faq.q: How is this different from a D&C?
faq.a: It is simpler: no anesthesia, no widening of the cervix, just a thin tube.

reminders.text: Endometrial biopsy tomorrow. Bring your ultrasound results and a pad. Ask your doctor about a painkiller beforehand.
